tool.name: microsim
tool.description: pore-scale pseudo-3D Stokes flow simulation from a PGM geometry

organization.name: Helmholtz Centre for Environmental Research - UFZ, Department of Technical Biogeochemistry

tool.command: #set $pixelsize_x_m = float($sim_params.pixelsize_x_um) * 1e-6 #set $pixelsize_y_m = float($sim_params.pixelsize_y_um) * 1e-6 #set $height_m = float($sim_params.height_um) * 1e-6 mkdir -p case_input case_output && cp '$pgm_file' 'case_input/geometry.pgm' && python3 '@DUMUX_PATH@/runStokesGeneric.py' -dir case_input -outdir case_output -input '@DUMUX_PATH@/genericInput.input' -vs_x $pixelsize_x_m -vs_y $pixelsize_y_m -height $height_m -dumux '@DUMUX_PATH@' -exec pseudo3D_stokes -govEq brinkman -no_lambda -heightAveraged -get_phi -vtu
tool.help:
.. class:: infomark
**What it does**
This tool runs the **Pseudo-3D-Stokes module for varying apertures**, a DuMux-based simulation module developed to help plan, improve, and interpret microfluidic experiments through numerical simulation of Stokes/Brinkman flow.
The pore geometry is given as an 8-bit grayscale PGM image, where each pixel encodes the local aperture of the microfluidic cell at that point: 0 is fully closed, 255 is fully open (the channel height you set below), and intermediate values represent partially open apertures. It then solves for the flow field on this pseudo-3D channel, driven by a fixed pressure difference between inlet and outlet.
**How to use it**
1. Upload or select a PGM geometry image as **PGM geometry**. 2. Under **Simulation parameters**, set the physical size a single pixel represents (**Pixel size in x/y**) and the **Channel height** - all in micrometers (µm). 3. Click **Run Tool**. 4. Once the job finishes, the output VTU file (named after your uploaded geometry) contains the converged pressure/velocity field and can be downloaded or opened with a VTK-aware viewer such as `ParaView <https://www.paraview.org/>`_.
**Input**
- **PGM geometry**: an 8-bit grayscale PGM pore/aperture geometry image. - **Pixel size in x / Pixel size in y**: physical size of one pixel, in µm. - **Channel height**: height of the pseudo-3D channel, in µm.
**Output**
A single VTU file holding the final (converged) timestep of the simulation (pressure and velocity fields).
**Publication**
If you use this tool in scientific work, please cite:
Krach D, Weinhardt F, Wang M, Schneider M, Class H, Steeb H. *A novel geometry-informed drag term formulation for pseudo-3D Stokes simulations with varying apertures.* Advances in Water Resources, 195 (2025). doi: `10.1016/j.advwatres.2024.104860 <https://doi.org/10.1016/j.advwatres.2024.104860>`_
Source code: `git.iws.uni-stuttgart.de/krachdd/pseudo3D_stokes <https://git.iws.uni-stuttgart.de/krachdd/pseudo3D_stokes>`_
**Contact / support**
- `Felix Weinhardt <mailto:felix.weinhardt@ufz.de>`_
**Note**
In this current version, the boundary conditions are fixed: the pressure difference between inlet and outlet is hard-coded to **1.4x10^-3 Pa (0.0014 Pa)**, and the resulting velocity field is whatever this fixed pressure difference produces for your geometry - it is not itself a free parameter. In upcoming versions, the pressure difference (and/or a target flow rate) are planned to be exposed as adjustable inputs.
